name: Turismo_Salento_forecasting
what_it_holds: `lecce_turismo_pulito.csv`: 760 rows x 27 columns of official Istat (Italian statistics institute) accommodation-movement data — arrivals, overnight stays, Italian vs. international visitor split, and average length of stay by year and municipality — for 92 municipalities in the Province of Lecce (Salento, Puglia), 2014-2024 annual. Also references a separate Naples Airbnb listings snapshot (9,752 listings, Sept 2025) used as a pricing proxy, and uses Facebook Prophet for dynamic-pricing forecasting.
why_useful: A committed, cleaned Italian municipal-level tourism accommodation panel (2014-2024) — a finer-grained, longer regional hotel/accommodation demand series than what we currently hold for Southern Italy, and a second independent Inside-Airbnb Naples pull that could be checked against our own IA captures for basis consistency.
size_hint: 760 rows x 27 cols processed CSV + Istat source worksheets referenced
themes: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data
why_all: A committed, cleaned Italian municipal-level tourism accommodation panel (2014-2024) — a finer-grained, longer regional hotel/accommodation demand series than what we currently hold for Southern Italy, and a second independent Inside-Airbnb Naples pull that could be checked against our own IA captures for basis consistency.

Real, municipality-level Istat tourism-flow data for an Italian region over an 11-year span plus a length-of-stay breakdown by nationality — could support cross-checking European regional-travel-demand patterns (gap #7/regulatory panel already holds Eurostat national-level `tour_ce_omr`; this is sub-national and includes length-of-stay, which Eurostat's monthly series does not break out at this granularity). Airbnb angle is a same-country different-city proxy only, not usable directly for ABNB but the length-of-stay/international-share variables are the more novel piece.

name: Spatial-hedonics-crime
what_it_holds: Stata + Python codebase estimating a spatial hedonic panel model of short-term-rental (Inside Airbnb-sourced) listing prices in Buenos Aires (CABA) against neighborhood crime rates and socioeconomic controls; >145,000 observations. Cleaned dataset also mirrored on Kaggle (marcodiazzz/buenos-aires-rentals-and-crime) for direct pull. Headline estimate: 1% rise in local crime -> 0.062% drop in STR price.
why_useful: A genuine academic-style hedonic pricing replication with committed code and a pullable dataset for a LatAm market (gap #7 geography) not in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; useful as a methods reference for hedonic/elasticity specification even though the target variable (crime, not bedroom/superhost mix) differs from our exact ask.
time_coverage: not stated in README excerpt; Inside Airbnb-derived snapshot(s)
themes: Airbnb and hotel price-elasticity, hedonic and mix-decomposition studies with data (bedroom counts, listing quality, superhost premium)
why_all: A genuine academic-style hedonic pricing replication with committed code and a pullable dataset for a LatAm market (gap #7 geography) not in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; useful as a methods reference for hedonic/elasticity specification even though the target variable (crime, not bedroom/superhost mix) differs from our exact ask.

name: airbnb_european_cities
what_it_holds: Uses a committed 'airbnb_european-cities.csv' (Rome and Berlin per README, but the file name matches the well-known 10-city 'Airbnb Prices in European Cities' Kaggle dataset lineage - Amsterdam/Athens/Barcelona/Berlin/Budapest/Lisbon/London/Paris/Rome/Vienna - which carries cleanliness_rating, guest_satisfaction_overall, host_is_superhost, distance-to-center and room_type fields not present in raw Inside Airbnb scrapes). Repo computes median price by room type, cleanliness-vs-satisfaction correlation, price-vs-distance profile, and an explicit superhost price premium calculation, with both notebook and script versions.
why_useful: A structured hedonic dataset with pre-computed listing-quality scores (cleanliness, guest satisfaction) and an explicit superhost premium calculation is closer to the theme's exact ask (bedroom/quality/superhost mix decomposition) than raw Inside Airbnb data; worth checking whether the underlying 10-city CSV (likely a static one-time snapshot, not point-in-time) is committed or externally sourced.
geography: European cities (Rome, Berlin per this repo; likely part of a broader 10-city Kaggle set)
duplicate_of_holding: Possibly a subset of a well-known static Kaggle Airbnb-Europe file; not the same as our Inside Airbnb 13-city panel (different cities, has satisfaction/cleanliness fields IA lacks)
